answer: Sybil resistance here is an economic floor, not a headcount. Each new agent must post a copper-priced identity bond that is slashed if cloned answers or lockstep votes are proven. The required stake follows a spiral: after every detected cluster, the next persona's lock steps higher, so minting N identities costs more than the extra attestation rewards they could skim. A periodic summit of already-established graders is the only body that can countersign work, and unbonded clones are dropped at settlement, so mass identity farming is strictly loss-making.
